key_decisions: SHAPES IS ARMED LIKE pointsMode, NOT AS A CANVAS MODE. `shapeMode` (null|'mask'|'paint') is a flag inside the canvas' existing mask/paint mode, so CANVAS_MODES and _enterMode were never touched and brush ownership, the undo gate and the paint render pass keep working underneath. This is the trap MPI-375 fell into (a dead tool that looked alive) and it was designed around, not discovered.

THE COMMIT LIVES ON THE LAYER MANAGERS, not on MpiCanvas: MaskManager.commitShape() and PaintManager.commitShape(), each taking a path BUILDER and applying its OWN _scale. The mask works at 1536 and paint at 4096 - a path built for one is silently offset in the other. It is also what keeps masking-undo.md's per-manager mutation table honest.

HIT-TESTING RUNS IN SHAPE-LOCAL SPACE - inverse-rotate the cursor, then run CropManager's axis-aligned test verbatim. One test serves all three kinds AND rotation. CropManager's handle keys, hit radius, drawing and cursor map are IMPORTED, not forked; if a change ever edits two handle systems, that extraction regressed.

SHIFT LOCKS THE RATIO THE SHAPE HAS, not the 1:1 seed (user's call, Figma behaviour not Photoshop's). ROTATION SNAPS TO 7.5 deg, snapping the ABSOLUTE angle so an off-grid shape squares back up, with the orbit using the same snapped delta or the pivot handle slides off the cursor.

THE SHAPE SURVIVES ITS COMMIT (stamp again by dragging) but an UNCOMMITTED gizmo is a preview: discardPreview() drops it, on the ONE seam, never at the mountOptions call site. MPI-373 hangs its preview on that same seam.

MPI-368 SHIPS FILLED-ONLY, and that is why MPI-436 exists. An outline mode on the gizmo would be a second, worse implementation of what Adjust's edge band already does - and it would only ever outline a shape, where _morph outlines any paint.
DOCS WERE SPLIT, NOT TRIMMED. masking-tools.md was 11 lines over its cap BEFORE this card and the remaining fat was measured evidence. Two new docs; masking-sam3.md was the precedent.
constraints: THE FINDING THIS SESSION DID NOT FIX. MaskManager.getURL() exports `a > 0` as solid white, while fillHoles() and the rest of the app cut at `>= 128`. Antialiasing means destination-out can never fully remove what an antialiased fill put down, so every erase leaves a sub-threshold rim that the export then promotes to REAL MASK. Measured at 2048 sq: a shape Add->Subtract leaves 1973 px non-zero and 0 px at 128; the SHIPPED MASK BRUSH leaves 1605 px and 0 at 128 after paint-then-erase. The brush number is the point - it predates MPI-368 and belongs to whoever owns the export threshold. getURL() is on the path of every masked generation, so brief before touching it. Detail: docs/masking-shapes.md and tasks/MPI-424/brief.md item 5.
